newsitem.title: GERMANY: German March ind output up 0.5 pct, driven by east.
newsitem.headline: German March ind output up 0.5 pct, driven by east.

text.p: German industrial production in March rose 0.5 percent from the previous month, driven by a sizable upturn in output in eastern Germany, the Economics Ministry said on Monday.
Production in the former communist east rose a seasonally adjusted 6.8 percent in March, while output in west Germany was virtually flat, showing an increase of only 0.1 percent.
Year-on-year, pan-German output rose 4.7 precent, according to calculations made by Reuters based on the official data.
West German production was up 3.2 percent and east German production up 13.9 percent compared to March 1996, the data showed.
Analysts said the gains remained moderate. Trinkhaus Capital Management said, "Since domestic demand remains relatively restrained, a strong turnaround in industry production is not be be expected."

Trinkhaus said it expected the weak consumer sector to limit real growth in Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) to 0.2 percent in the first quarter. It expected 2.0 percent growth for the full year.
Month-on-month gains in eastern Germany stemmed from a 14.3 percent climb in capital-goods production and a 13.8 percent increase in construction output.

The gain in construction came after severe winter weather limited output in the previous months, Trinkhaus said. The weakening of the mark against the dollar also boosted output, the investment company said.
In west Germany, capital-goods production fell 3.2 percent compared to February, while mining output dropped 3.8 percent, the Economics Ministry reported.
Offsetting those setbacks, durable-goods production increased 5.8 percent month-on-month, while consumer-goods production increased 2.8 percent and construction 3.0 percent.
